name: Gastric Acid Secretion and Parietal Cell Physiology

reference.source: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology / Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology
clinicalPearls: Parietal cells in gastric oxyntic glands secrete hydrochloric acid (pH ~1.5) and intrinsic factor (for cobalamin absorption)
Proton pump (H+/K+ ATPase) secretes H+ in exchange for K+ at apical canalicular membrane; basolateral HCO3-/Cl- creates alkaline tide
Three secretagogues stimulate acid: Histamine (paracrine from ECL cells via H2/cAMP), Acetylcholine (vagus via M3/Ca2+), Gastrin (G cells via CCK-B/Ca2+)
Somatostatin from antral D cells acts as master inhibitor via Gi/SST2 receptors when luminal pH falls below 3.0
Proton pump inhibitors (omeprazole) form covalent disulphide bonds with H+/K+ ATPase, irreversibly blocking the final common pathway
reference.pathophysiology: Helicobacter pylori antral gastritis destroys D cells, decreasing somatostatin and disinhibiting gastrin release, producing hyperchlorhydria and duodenal ulceration. Autoimmune metaplastic atrophic gastritis destroys parietal cells via anti-parietal cell and anti-intrinsic factor antibodies, causing achlorhydria, compensatory hypergastrinemia and pernicious anemia.
additionalInvestigations: Fasting serum gastrin measurement (>1000 pg/mL suggests gastrinoma)
Secretin stimulation test (paradoxical gastrin rise confirms Zollinger-Ellison)
Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with antral and corpus biopsies
